item.content:encoded:
Robert Downey Jr’s son bags first lead role in film titled ‘Love in Vein’ Written and directed by Will De Los Santos, the film is based on the late Ryan Leone’s novel ‘Wasting Talent’. The story follows Damien, played by Indio, as he deals with addiction, relationships and the struggles of life in Los Angeles. ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 09:38 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 09:38 IST

Robert Downey Jr (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Indio Downey, son of Hollywood actor Robert Downey Jr., is set to play the lead role in the upcoming independent film ‘Love In Vein’. The film, which deals with addiction, love and self-destruction, will mark Indio’s first lead role in a movie, Deadline reported. Written and directed by Will De Los Santos, the film is based on the late Ryan Leone’s novel ‘Wasting Talent’. The story follows Damien, played by Indio, as he deals with addiction, relationships and the struggles of life in Los Angeles. The film will be produced by Muse Productions in association with ArtHouse Gooning. Shooting is scheduled to take place in Los Angeles in March and April 2027. Casting for other roles is currently underway. Chris Hanley, known for producing films such as ‘American Psycho’, ‘Spring Breakers’ and ‘The Virgin Suicides’, will produce the film alongside Orson Oblowitz, Tricia van Klaveren and Ben D. Wallace. Jeffrey Gliwa is financing the project through Blue Shark Pictures and will also serve as an executive producer. Speaking about the film, director Will De Los Santos said he wanted to stay true to the original novel and its subject matter. He also spoke about how the author’s death had given the project a deeper meaning. “Ryan left behind a brutally honest novel about addiction, love and Los Angeles. Since his passing, making Love In Vein has taken on an even deeper meaning for me. I want to honor his voice and the rawness of the book without softening its edges,” said De Los Santos, as per the publication. Indio, 33, is a musician and the eldest of Robert Downey Jr.’s three children. He has previously appeared in a few films, including ‘Kiss Kiss Bang Bang’, which starred his father. However, ‘Love In Vein’ will be his first film in a lead role. Robert Downey Jr. has also spoken publicly about his past struggles with addiction. He later rebuilt his career and became one of Hollywood’s leading actors, according to Deadline. (ANI)

item.title: US Congressman Krishnamoorthi leads 256 cosponsors in resolution to designate July as 'Indian American Heritage Month'
item.description: US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi has introduced a bipartisan resolution, backed by 256 cosponsors, honouring the contributions of Indian Americans and supporting the designation of July as 'Indian ...
item.content:encoded:
US Congressman Krishnamoorthi leads 256 cosponsors in resolution to designate July as 'Indian American Heritage Month' US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi has introduced a bipartisan resolution, backed by 256 cosponsors, honouring the contributions of Indian Americans and supporting the designation of July as 'Indian American Heritage Month'. ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 09:34 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 09:34 IST

US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi has introduced a bipartisan resolution, backed by 256 cosponsors, honouring the contributions of Indian Americans and supporting the designation of July as 'Indian American Heritage Month'. According to a press release issued by Krishnamoorthi's office on Monday (local time), the resolution recognises the contributions of more than 5.2 million Indian Americans to the United States across fields including science and medicine, technology and business, public service and the military, education, philanthropy, arts and culture, and athletics. "Indian Americans have helped shape this country for generations, from breakthroughs that have saved lives and businesses that have created jobs to lifetimes of service in our military and public office," Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. "I'm proud to lead 256 of my colleagues in designating July as Indian American Heritage Month to honor that legacy and celebrate the many ways Indian Americans continue to enrich our country," he added. The proposed resolution, submitted by Krishnamoorthi in the US House of Representatives during the second session of the 119th Congress, has been referred to a House committee for consideration, according to the resolution. The resolution notes that, according to estimates published by the US Census Bureau in 2023, more than 5.2 million people in the United States identify as Indian American. It highlights the community's historical and cultural roots, noting that Indian Americans trace their roots to "a civilization more than 5,000 years old" and have brought to the United States "a rich legacy of art, literature, philosophy, science, and democratic traditions". The proposed designation of July commemorates the signing of the Luce-Celler Act by then US President Harry S.Truman on July 2, 1946. The legislation made people of Indian descent eligible for naturalisation as US citizens. The resolution also recognises the religious diversity of Indian Americans, stating that they represent "a wide range of faith traditions that strengthen the Nation's cultural and spiritual fabric". Highlighting their public service, the resolution notes that Indian Americans "have served with distinction at all levels of government and public service, including in every branch of the United States Armed Forces". It further acknowledges their contributions to science and technology, stating that Indian Americans "have made pioneering contributions to science, medicine, biomedical research, space exploration, artificial intelligence, computing, telecommunications, and other fields of innovation that have improved lives and expanded human knowledge". The resolution also highlights their role in business, education, journalism and philanthropy, stating that Indian Americans have contributed to "the economic strength, intellectual life, and global leadership of the United States". Recognising their cultural contributions, the resolution text stated that Indian Americans "have enriched the cultural fabric of the United States through music, film, television, the performing arts, cuisine, athletics, and the preservation and sharing of India's diverse cultural, religious, linguistic, and regional traditions". Emphasising the purpose of the proposed observance, the resolution states that July provides an opportunity to recognise "the history, achievements, cultural traditions, and diverse religious and regional identities of Indian Americans" and celebrate their many contributions to the United States. The resolution in the end stated that the US House of Representatives "recognizes that Indian Americans enhance the rich diversity and strength of the United States" and supports the designation of "Indian American Heritage Month". (ANI)

item.title: ‘Star Trek’ actor Walter Koenig passes away at 90
item.description: Veteran actor Walter Koenig, best known for portraying Pavel Andreievich Chekov in the original “Star Trek” television series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, has passed away at the age of 90.
item.content:encoded:
‘Star Trek’ actor Walter Koenig passes away at 90 Veteran actor Walter Koenig, best known for portraying Pavel Andreievich Chekov in the original “Star Trek” television series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, has passed away at the age of 90. ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 09:35 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 09:35 IST

Late actor Walter Koenig (Image source: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Veteran actor Walter Koenig, best known for portraying Pavel Andreievich Chekov in the original “Star Trek” television series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, has passed away at the age of 90. According to The Hollywood Reporter, Koenig’s representative announced that the actor died of natural causes at his home on Sunday. Born and raised in Manhattan to Lithuanian immigrant parents, Koenig joined Gene Roddenberry’s 'Star Trek'  at the beginning of its second season. He appeared in 36 of the 50 episodes broadcast during the 1967–68 and 1968–69 seasons, portraying Russian navigator Pavel Andreievich Chekov. Koenig went on to reprise the role in the first seven “Star Trek” feature films released by Paramount between 1979 and 1991. His contributions to the franchise earned him widespread recognition among science fiction fans. In a 2013 interview for the TV Academy Foundation, Koenig revealed that he didn’t watch Star Trek before he came aboard. “I’d flip through the channels and I’d see Styrofoam rocks — they were so obviously Styrofoam — and I said, ‘This has got to be phony.’ I didn’t give it a chance,” he recalled. Before joining “Star Trek”, Koenig had appeared in several television productions. In 1963, he portrayed a student who had defected to the United States in an episode of the NBC drama “Mr. Novak”, marking the first time he played a Russian character in his career. In 1964, he guest-starred in an episode of “The Lieutenant”, another series created by Roddenberry. He portrayed a young sergeant aspiring to become an officer, whose ambitions were complicated by the fact that his mother was a communist. Koenig’s contributions to the Star Trek film franchise earned him greater recognition, including nominations from the Academy of Science Fiction, Fantasy & Horror Films for his performances in Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan (1982) and Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home (1986). On the personal front, Koenig married actress Judy Levitt in July 1965. Levitt appeared alongside him in three “Star Trek” films and also featured in “Babylon 5”. The couple remained together until her death in December 2022 at the age of 83. Their son, Andrew Koenig, was known for playing Richard “Boner” Stabone on the ABC sitcom “Growing Pains”. He died by suicide in 2010 at the age of 41.(ANI)

item.title: US STOCKS-Wall St eyes best day in a month as Anthropic's IPO filing propels AI stocks
item.description: Read more about US STOCKS-Wall St eyes best day in a month as Anthropic's IPO filing propels AI stocks on Devdiscourse ...
item.content:encoded:
US STOCKS-Wall St eyes best day in a month as Anthropic's IPO filing propels AI stocks Reuters | Updated: 26-10-2026 21:34 IST | Created: 26-10-2026 21:34 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set for their biggest one-day gain in more than a month on Monday as tech stocks advanced after Anthropic's IPO filing put AI back in focus at the start of a week packed with corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision. Anthropic disclosed steep losses and red-hot revenue growth in its filing for a US initial public offering, laying out its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology. The AI lab is pushing ahead with its listing plans even as a once-busy fall IPO calendar has thinned out, with market volatility prompting companies to delay offerings. "It's a challenging environment to say the least exactly when this IPO will take place, but there's a lot riding on not only the company, but the AI industry," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield. Semiconductor and chip-related companies, widely viewed as some of the biggest winners of the AI boom, were leading the gains. The broader Philadelphia chips index was up more than 3% after a turbulent few weeks. Anthropic's filing arrives as investors increasingly scrutinize the payoff from AI spending. About a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including hyperscalers Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon.com, whose results would be parsed for signs if the hefty AI investments are translating into growth. The focus follows a subdued reception to earnings from AI-linked megacaps last week. Meta disappointed investors after raising its annual AI spending forecast again and saying it would sell new stock to help pay for it, while Tesla also came under pressure following its results. Meta said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity to fund its AI-related expansion of data centers, cloud computing power and other infrastructure. Its shares were last up 0.2%. The AI trade has come under pressure this month amid concerns that debt-funded spending may become harder to justify in the face of rising borrowing costs. Sentiment, however, improved a bit on Monday as neocloud firms such as CoreWeave and Nebius, which have been at the center of the AI storm, reversed initial losses to trade higher. Other AI-linked companies, including photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent, along with server makers Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, were among the best-performing stocks. At 11:30 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 168.52 points, or 0.32%, to 52,383.68. The S&P 500 gained 70.17 points, or 0.92%, to 7,693.85, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 325.16 points, or 1.25%, to 26,280.50. Market breadth was strong, with eight of the 11 S&P 500 sectors trading higher. Information technology and consumer discretionary led the gains. Megacap and growth stocks were also mostly higher. Tesla jumped 6.3% to a more than three-month high after Barclays upgraded its rating on the stock to "overweight" from "equal-weight". Crude oil prices eased after hitting a near six-month high last week. On Sunday, Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran as part of an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the United States. Elsewhere, the Fed's rate decision is due on Wednesday, with a pause widely expected after its September raise. Traders still see a December hike as firmly possible, and at least two 25-basis-point increases by mid-2027, according to LSEG data. Both the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — the Personal Consumption Expenditures index for September, and third-quarter GDP, expected to show 3.2% growth — are due on Thursday. Investors are also monitoring the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the US Congress. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.07-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.56-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted six new 52-week highs and five new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 69 new highs and 262 new lows.
